  nameable fact — read the file and name the operator or bound that is actually
  there. Do not describe the failure as "logic error" when you can name the line.
- Because the diagnosis names a checkable fact, target=none is almost always
  WRONG for this project. A retry cannot rediscover an operator it already got
  wrong once. Use target=skill and state the operator or bound explicitly.
- Both codelines already declare vitest and typescript. A "cannot find module" or
  "not installed" claim about either is suspicious — verify with your tools before
  believing it. Do not reach for target=tool to install a dependency that is
  already declared.

  test files. A path confusion between mock-a and mock-b (editing src/fares.ts
  when the failing test is test/schedule.test.ts, or vice versa) is a real failure
  mode for an implementer that spans both — check which codeline the failing test
  actually lives in before diagnosing the code.
- Off-by-one fixes are easy to over-apply: flipping a bound can turn "omits the
  last stop" into "emits one past the end" (undefined / trailing separator), and
  flipping an age operator can move the bug from 65 to 64. If the failure output
  shows the boundary moved rather than closed, say so — that is a different
  diagnosis than the original bug.

Decision rules:
- target=prd: the AC wording was ambiguous or contradictory, causing the agent to write wrong code. Fix the AC.
  Here that usually means an AC that says "riders over 65" or "up to the last stop"
  without stating whether the boundary value is included — inclusive/exclusive
  ambiguity is the characteristic PRD defect for these two tickets.
- target=tc: the testCriteria facts are wrong or incomplete — the test agent followed them but they described incorrect behavior. Fix the TC facts.
  Here that usually means a TC fact that asserts the wrong side of the boundary
  (age 64 or 66 instead of exactly 65), or omits the boundary case entirely.
- target=skill: the agent used a bad coding pattern that should be injected into this retry's prompt only. This INCLUDES any diagnosis that names a specific, checkable fact about a type, property, field, or signature (e.g. "missing required X field", "Config doesn't match Y's type", "wrong argument count for Z") — that fact will not change no matter how many times or how strong a model you retry with, so it must be told, not re-guessed.
  A named comparison operator or loop bound counts as such a fact. Carry the exact
  file path and the exact operator or bound in the note.
- target=kb: the failure reveals a reusable coding rule that ALL future agents with this agent role should know — append to the role-specific KB.
- target=tool: the failure is a repeated MECHANICAL step (not a knowledge gap) that a small shell script can perform reliably every time — e.g. "add a dependency to this codeline's manifest (__MANIFEST_FILE__) and install it before importing it". Only use target=tool when a KB rule alone has already failed to prevent the same class of failure, or the fix is a multi-step shell recipe error-prone to repeat by hand. Provide tool_spec.
  Expect this to be rare in mock3: both codelines declare only vitest and
  typescript, and a one-line boundary fix is a knowledge gap, not a mechanical step.
- target=none: reserved for a genuinely non-reproducible mistake — a stray typo, a one-off slip with no identifiable pattern — where your own diagnosis does not name a specific, checkable, nameable fact (a property, type, field, or signature) that a future attempt could look up and get right. If your diagnosis DOES name such a fact, that is deterministic, not transient, and target=none is the wrong answer even if you are uncertain what the exact correct value should be — use target=skill and describe the fact you found, even incompletely, rather than defaulting to a retry that cannot discover it on its own.
- Only include ac_patches when target=prd, tc_patches when target=tc; use [] for other targets. Only include tool_spec when target=tool; omit otherwise.
- skill_note must be AT MOST __SKILL_NOTE_MAX__ characters. It is injected into a retry prompt and may persist into the agent's profile, so a note past that length is rejected and has to be rewritten before the retry can use it — write within it the first time.
- skill_note must be a concrete "do/don't" instruction, written so it can be ACTED ON without further interpretation:
  * OPEN WITH AN IMPERATIVE VERB (Use, Always, Never, Prefer, Avoid). A note opening with a subordinate clause ("When integrating X, ...") is reformatted before storage, which costs a round trip and risks losing detail.
  * STATE THE RULE COMPLETELY. A note that stops mid-sentence is worse than no note, because the reader cannot tell it is incomplete and will act on the fragment.
  * CARRY ANY LITERAL VERBATIM AND UNABBREVIATED — a regex, a path, a command, a flag, a config value. Never elide one with "..." or "e.g.", and never shorten it to save space. THE LITERAL IS THE FIX; the prose around it is not actionable without it.
    For this project the literal is the operator or the bound: write `age >= 65`,
    not "the age check"; write `i < stops.length`, not "the loop bound". Include
    the file path (src/fares.ts or src/schedule.ts) so the right codeline is edited.
  * If the complete literal will not fit alongside the explanation, KEEP THE LITERAL AND SHORTEN THE EXPLANATION. Never the reverse.
  * Example: "Never use backtick template literals in test files — use single-quoted strings only."
- tool_spec.recipe must be idempotent shell — safe to run more than once (e.g. check before installing).
- Keep diagnosis under 20 words, reason under 15 words.
